- **Recording:** He recorded it at Cosimo Matassa's J&M Recording Studio in New Orleans, where the young Ray Charles arranged and produced the session. One discography dates the session to Dec 1953.

results:
The search found no single 1953 release featuring all three singers. It did turn up 1953 recordings by Bennett and Sinatra, and only a later compilation for Fitzgerald.

- **Tony Bennett:** His 1953 single "Rags to Riches" came out on Columbia with Percy Faith's orchestra, according to a WFMU playlist listing. It reached No. 6 on the Billboard-style chart dated November 21, 1953.
- **Frank Sinatra:** His 1953 Capitol releases included "I've Got the World on a String," listed as the B-side of "South of the Border" on a 10" shellac. "Same Old Saturday Night" was also a hit that year, and Sinatra Sings His Greatest Hits appeared in the 1953 music listings.
- **Ella Fitzgerald:** I found no original 1953 release. A 2006 AllMusic compilation titled *1953-1954* gathers her recordings from February 13, 1953 - March 30, 1954, so those tracks were recorded in 1953 but released later.

The sources are uneven. The Sinatra and Bennett entries come from playlists and chart listings, so I'd verify them against a discography such as Discogs before relying on exact release details.
